data.name: Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy
data.detailed_description:
Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy is a strategy game of 3D tactical space battles. Play your part in the Second Contact War in a campaign with a branching story and over 60 missions, or create your own scenarios in skirmish mode battles!



The Universe is a Dangerous Place. In the 22nd century, we left a dying earth so that a fortunate few could settle the new home we call Novus. In time, we would learn that life on a frontier colony is neither prosperous nor peaceful. Our first encounter with the nautilid started with hostilities and confusion, and ended with sacrifice. Fourteen years later, our leaders remain politically entangled and unable to see the threats that linger, both afar and within our own walls…

Give your orders, and watch the results in explosive pausable real-time. Tailor your arsenal of crew abilities and assault class ships as your fleet grows with your command. Exploit the enemy’s weaknesses with superior positioning and flanking manoeuvres to inflict devastating damage.

Six classes of assaults ships are yours to command. Make precision strikes with the swift Swordfish Raiders, or lead from the bridge of a hulking Kraken Dreadnought. Change your tactics as you order reinforcements with stun guns, guided missiles, unmanned fighter drones and single-focus DEW beams.

The nautilid threat is as varied as it is innumerable, however, and they will not surrender. Use your wits to overcome the threat of disruption fields, bio-missiles and proximity mines. And not all opposition to your command comes from outside. Raise the shields of your capital ships and engage in devastating broadside combat with the renegade military conspiracists who call themselves the Remnant.

Manage your crew’s personalities and morale to tailor your flagship’s advantage in battle. Every crew member you enlist has their own personality traits, abilities and stories. Measure your actions against the War Scale. Will your command be a legacy of calculated tactical bombardments, or aggressive and reckless assaults? Take part in an ongoing war with no turning back. Choose who will be saved, order reinforcements to replace destroyed veteran ships, and shape the future of mankind’s second home.

Will you obey the chain of command and strengthen Novus’ defenses, or take your opponents head-on by yourself?

FEATURES


  • Fight for Novus and decide the outcome of the Second Contact War with a branching story that boasts over 60 missions.
  • WeGo tactical combat in 3D space, with gameplay that rewards strategic positioning and fleet coordination. Give your commands, then watch the results in pausable realtime.
  • Take command of a range of heavily armed assault ships, including Raiders, Corvettes, Frigates, Destroyers, Battlecruisers and Dreadnoughts - each with with their own weapons fitouts and unique functions.
  • Balance the energy core of each ship to focus on impenetrable defences, breakneck piloting or devastating assaults.
  • Manage your crew’s personalities and morale to tailor your flagship’s advantage in battle. Every crew member you enlist has their own personality traits, abilities and stories.
  • Measure your actions against the War Scale. Will your command be a legacy of calculated tactical bombardments, or aggressive and reckless assaults
  • Take part in an ongoing war with no turning back. Choose who will be saved, order reinforcements to replace destroyed veteran ships, and shape the future of mankind’s second home.

data.short_description: Take command of Naval Strike Group 7 and lead your fleet to victory in full 3D tactical space combat. Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy is a sci-fi strategy saga that will test your skills as both capital assault ship Captain and naval fleet Commander.

reviews.review:
Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy is a tactical space combat strategy game developed by Black Lab Games and published by Slitherine Ltd. that offers a thoughtful and highly strategic take on fleet warfare in a futuristic science-fiction setting. Rather than emphasizing fast-paced action or large-scale empire building, the game focuses on carefully planned engagements where every movement, attack order, and tactical decision can determine the outcome of a battle. Combining turn-based planning with simultaneous real-time execution, Star Hammer delivers a unique command experience that rewards patience, foresight, and intelligent fleet management.

Set in a future where humanity has spread beyond Earth in search of survival, the game presents a military science-fiction universe filled with political tension, interstellar conflict, and an ongoing war against a powerful alien threat. The campaign centers on humanity's efforts to defend its colonies and maintain stability during a dangerous period known as the Second Contact War. While the story embraces familiar genre themes such as survival, military duty, and alien conflict, it provides a solid framework that gives purpose to the numerous fleet engagements players will face throughout the campaign.

The game's defining feature is its innovative combat system. Instead of taking turns one after another, both sides issue commands simultaneously before watching them unfold in real time. This creates a constant sense of uncertainty because players cannot simply react to enemy actions after seeing them happen. Success depends on anticipating an opponent's intentions, positioning ships effectively, and committing to strategies before knowing exactly how the enemy will respond. The result is a combat system that feels closer to commanding an actual military operation than a conventional strategy game.

Positioning plays a critical role in every engagement. Battles occur within fully three-dimensional environments where fleets maneuver across multiple layers of space. Ships can attack from different angles, use terrain for protection, and exploit gaps in enemy formations. Asteroid fields, debris clouds, and other environmental features become important tactical considerations rather than simple visual decoration. Mastering movement and spatial awareness often proves just as important as selecting the right weapons.

Fleet composition adds another layer of strategic depth. Players command a variety of vessels, including corvettes, frigates, cruisers, carriers, and specialized support ships. Each class serves a distinct purpose on the battlefield. Smaller vessels offer speed and flexibility, while larger ships provide firepower and durability. Support units contribute electronic warfare capabilities, fighter deployment, and logistical assistance. Building a balanced fleet requires understanding how these different roles interact and support one another during combat.

One of the game's strengths is the sense of ownership it creates over individual ships and crews. Throughout the campaign, players recruit officers and specialists who provide valuable bonuses and unique abilities. These personnel can significantly influence combat performance, making their survival an important consideration. Over time, fleets begin to develop their own identity, and players often become attached to veteran crews that have survived multiple difficult engagements.

The campaign offers substantial content, featuring dozens of missions spread across a branching storyline. Player decisions influence progression, and combat performance can affect future opportunities and rewards. This structure adds replay value by encouraging experimentation with different tactical approaches. Some missions emphasize direct confrontation, while others require defensive operations, escort duties, reconnaissance tasks, or survival against overwhelming odds. The variety helps maintain engagement throughout the lengthy campaign.

An especially interesting feature is the game's strategic progression system, which rewards different styles of command. Players who favor aggressive tactics may unlock different benefits than those who prioritize defense and caution. These choices influence resource management and campaign development, making overall strategy just as important as individual battles.

The visual presentation succeeds in capturing the scale of interstellar warfare. Ship designs are distinctive, weapon effects are satisfying, and large engagements frequently produce impressive displays of missiles, lasers, explosions, and fighter attacks. While the graphics may not match the spectacle of major-budget space simulations, the battlefield remains visually engaging and effectively communicates the chaos and intensity of fleet combat.

Sound design further enhances immersion. Weapon impacts carry weight, engine effects help establish the presence of massive warships, and the soundtrack supports the game's military atmosphere. The music complements both the quieter planning phases and the more dramatic moments of combat, helping reinforce the tension that defines the experience.

One of the most commendable aspects of Star Hammer is its accessibility. Despite featuring complex mechanics and a unique combat system, the game introduces its concepts through a well-designed tutorial structure. New players gradually learn the fundamentals without being overwhelmed by information. At the same time, experienced strategy fans will find plenty of depth to explore as they master advanced fleet tactics and battlefield positioning.

The game is not entirely without flaws. The campaign narrative, while interesting, occasionally lacks the emotional impact necessary to make every character memorable. Some interface elements can feel cumbersome during larger engagements, and the deliberate pace of combat may not appeal to players looking for constant action. Additionally, the absence of multiplayer limits the longevity for those seeking competitive fleet battles.

However, these issues do little to undermine the quality of the core gameplay. Star Hammer excels because it understands exactly what it wants to be: a tactical command simulator where careful planning and intelligent decision-making matter more than reflexes. Every successful maneuver feels rewarding because victories are earned through strategy rather than overwhelming force.

What ultimately sets Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy apart is its commitment to meaningful tactical warfare. The combination of simultaneous-turn combat, three-dimensional battlefields, fleet customization, and campaign progression creates a distinctive strategy experience that remains engaging from beginning to end. Few space combat games manage to capture the feeling of commanding a military fleet with such precision and authenticity.

For fans of science-fiction strategy games, tactical warfare, and fleet-based combat, Star Hammer: The Vanguard Prophecy is an underrated gem that deserves far more attention than it received. Its intelligent design, satisfying battles, and emphasis on strategic thinking make it one of the more rewarding space warfare titles available. While it may not offer the scale of grand strategy games or the spectacle of action-oriented space simulators, it excels in delivering thoughtful and highly satisfying tactical combat.

Rating: 7/10
